NEW ROUND-2-FIX CLAIMS RE-DERIVED, all exact unless noted: release's step-6.5 sync at release.go:315-318 (guarded `if haveCursor && epicID != "" && active == beadID` wrapping `phase.DerivePhase` + `deps.syncPhase`) with the default syncPhase at release.go:151-153 merge-writing mindspec_phase; DerivePhase (derive.go:151) chains into the stored-trusting core at derive.go:174-193, so the R3.1 second-route claim (release preserves stored implement on the all-open set, the DerivePhase call emits the stored-vs-derived warning + repair hint, and the sync re-writes the stored value) is code-consistent; internal/journal's acquireFileLock exists with exactly the described platform split (lock_unix.go:22 flock(2) LOCK_EX; lock_windows.go:25 O_EXCL lockfile) and withReportsLock's held-across-read-modify-write pattern sits at lock.go:55-61 as cited; next.go:80 is the `resolve.ResolveSpecPrefix(specFlag)` call; TestResolveSpecPrefix_FullIDPassthrough exists at internal/resolve/target_test.go:162; the silent global-fallback citations are exact on both paths (claim path falls back to `next.QueryReady()` at next.go:166 when FindEpicBySpecID errors or returns empty, emit-only path identically at :417-424), so R6.7's behavioral characterization is true as written. ONE NEW GROUNDING DEFECT, the reason for this verdict: R3.3's lock-holder enumeration claims completeness ('held ... by every other mindspec_phase writer (enumerated at this base: plan approve's write at plan.go:455, complete's step-6.5 sync, release's step-6.5 sync at release.go:315-318, and the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write)') but the tree has more writers: `spec approve` merge-writes `mindspec_phase: "plan"` onto an existing epic at internal/approve/spec.go:76 (and seeds it in the creation metadata at :84), and the ADR-0034 migration writer `EnsureMigrated` merge-writes the derived phase at internal/phase/migrate.go:60 - and per ADR-0041 the migration runs ahead of every preflight in the very verbs the lock is meant to serialize, and it fires exactly when stored phase is absent, which is a state repair phase can also act on. Additionally 'the impl approve/impl adopt terminal write' is three distinct sites (impl.go:578's needsPhaseReconcile write - not terminal - plus impl.go:612's done write and adopt.go:424). The normative sentence ('every other mindspec_phase writer') is sound, but the 'enumerated at this base' parenthetical is a factual claim the tree refutes, and it is load-bearing: an implementer trusting it would leave real writers outside the critical section, silently voiding the round-2 G6 invariant the enumeration exists to deliver. That is a substantive grounding error, not a cosmetic offset, so this round is REQUEST_CHANGES.

findings.title: R3.3's 'enumerated at this base' mindspec_phase-writer list omits two real writers (spec approve, EnsureMigrated)
findings.detail: The round-2 G6 lock invariant requires the critical section be held by every mindspec_phase writer, and the spec asserts the writer set is 'enumerated at this base' as four items. Grep of the tree (non-test) shows seven write sites across six writers: plan.go:455 (listed), complete.go:1366 (listed), release.go:151-153/:315-318 (listed), impl.go:578 + :612 and adopt.go:424 (glossed as one 'terminal write' - :578 is a non-terminal reconcile write), internal/approve/spec.go:76/:84 (NOT listed), and internal/phase/migrate.go:60 (NOT listed). The migration writer is particularly relevant: it merge-writes exactly when stored phase is absent, runs ahead of the preflights in the lifecycle verbs per ADR-0041's migration exemption, and could interleave with a repair-phase invocation on the same epic - the precise class the lock exists to serialize. The enumeration must be corrected or the completeness claim withdrawn in favor of a plan-time re-derivation instruction.
